section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: In order to address certain issues with fonts which 'overhang' their right hand edge (such as oblique or italic fonts), a new flag bit has been added to Wimp_TextOp 1 (read size of string). This allows applications (such as the Filer) to calculate icon bounding boxes more reliably where such fonts are in use.

Since RISC OS 4 a number of additional flags have been available for Wimp_TextOp 2 (plot string). These allow the text strings to be rendered within the current window and make the font appear vertically centred at the position specified.
Two additional reason codes have been added to centralise the splitting of system font text and its truncation.

section.title: Technical Details
section.p: The operation is selected by the reason code in R0 bits 0-7:

bitfield-table.bit:
Operation:
Set colours to use Read string size Plot font Find split point in string Truncate string with ellipsis

section.p: Other registers are dependent on the operation. The SWI is used to perform text string operations using the desktop font.

swi-definition.name: Wimp_TextOp
swi-definition.description: Set colours for desktop font operations

use.p: This SWI sets the colours to use for subsequent desktop font operations.

swi-definition.name: Wimp_TextOp
swi-definition.description: Read the width of a string in the desktop font

entry.register-use:
1 (read string size) + flags:
Return size covered by string
Number of characters to process, or 0 for the entire string

exit.register-use: Width of string in desktop font in OS units

use.p: This SWI is used to read the width of a string when rendered on the screen. Bit 31 controls whether the space covered by the string is returned rather than the baseline offset at which the string ends. This distinction must be made because certain fonts (italic fonts, for example) will end at a baseline position before the end of the rendered font. With the bit set the whole area covered will be returned. Thus, if this call is required for locating the end of a string such that another may be added (for example, in another colour) then bit 31 should be clear. If, however, this call is being used to calculate the size required for the font such that it is entirely rendered (for example, in calculating the size of an icon's bounding box), bit 31 should be set.

swi-definition.name: Wimp_TextOp
swi-definition.description: Plot a text string in the desktop font

entry.register-use:
2 (plot text string) + flags:
Reserved, must be 0 Reserved for future expansion Centre text vertically X/Y offsets are offsets within the current redraw window, rather than screen offsets Vertically justify to make the baseline the same as system font Right justify string

use.p: This SWI is used to plot a text string in the desktop font.

swi-definition.name: Wimp_TextOp
swi-definition.description: Find the split point in a string

entry.register-use: Width to split at in OS units

exit.register-use: Pointer to split point in supplied string

use.p: This SWI is used to read a split point by limiting to a given length. It is similar in function to the SWI.

swi-definition.name: Wimp_TextOp
swi-definition.description: Truncate a string with an ellipsis

entry.register-use: Size of output buffer, or 0 to request size required

use.p: This SWI is used to truncate a string by using an ellipsis character for the currently selected alphabet, or three full stops. If the string fits within the size specified, no ellipsis will be added.
